label: sec:symmetric-point-preamble
html: The mass-gap conjecture locates the vanishing of the gap on the 2-torsion locus \mu_2 = \{1, -1\} \subset \mathbb{G}_m. This section examines the symmetric point q = 1 directly. We determine which structures of the mass tower \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n) survive the specialisation, which degenerate, and at what order in h = q - 1 each lost structure restores when the deformation switches back on. The pattern is uniform. The symmetric point deletes no spectrum, but loses resolution. Distinctions that braiding maintains—chirality of crossings, inter-nucleon channel identity, accidental level coincidences—collapse at q = 1 and reopen at definite infinitesimal orders.
